newsitem.title: ETHIOPIA: French firm starts construction of $25 mln brewery.
newsitem.headline: French firm starts construction of $25 mln brewery.

text.p: A Paris-based firm on Friday started construction of a new $25 million brewery in northern Ethiopia, the first major French investment in the Horn of Africa nation, the French embassy announced.
Commercial counsellor Didier Bourjuignon said that French firm Brasserie et Glacieres Internationale (BGI) of the Castel group had begun the project at Kombolcha, north of the capital.
Bourjuignon said the project was being funded by the French company, in a move hailed by local officials as an endorsement of the country's market reforms.

The government of Prime Minister Meles Zenawi, which overthrew Marxist dictator Mengistu Haile Mariam in 1991, has introduced a western-backed free market programme designed to end poverty and build growth.
The brewery is expected to produce up to 250,000 hectolitres of beer per year once completed next year.
Kombolcha Brewery will be the fifth in Ethiopia. Others include Meta Brewery, St.George Brewery, Bedle Brewery and Harar Brewery.

Bourjuignon said the Kombolcha project is the first investment venture for the CASTEL group in east Africa. It has built breweries, mineral water factories and wine processing plants in North, South and West African countries, he added.
